question: How many seats will PP and Vox collectively receive in the 2026 Spanish general election?

calls.reasoning: Polling average (politpro) PP 31.2, Vox 18.6 => ~50% combined vs 45.5% in 2023 (170 seats). Recent seat projections for PP+Vox: EM-Analytics 194/196, IMOP 195, GAD3 198, Sigma Dos 197-205, SocioMetrica 205, Hamalgama 212, CIS ~185; El Debate median of 12 pollsters 203 (Sept-early Oct). Shade median to ~195 for slight late-October softening of PP, the 2023 precedent of polls overstating the right bloc by ~10-15 seats, and late campaign mobilization of the left. Markets: Polymarket PP-most-seats ~0.76-0.78 (vol ~77k-171k), Kalshi Feijóo PM 78% — near-miss contracts, consistent with a right-bloc majority but not a seat-total anchor. No market on the combined seat count found.
calls.dossier:
- Election 29 Nov 2026; 350-seat Congress, majority 176; campaign 13-27 Nov (riotimesonline, Oct 25).
- 2023 result: PP 137, Vox 33 = 170 seats on 33.1%+12.4% vote. Pre-election 2023 polls had PP+Vox around 180+, so they overstated by ~10-15 seats.
- Politpro average (Oct 25): PP 31.2%, PSOE 26.0%, Vox 18.6%, Sumar 6.1%.
- Wikipedia poll table, PP+Vox seats: EM-Analytics 17-23 Oct 132+62=194; EM 15-17 Oct 134+62=196; IMOP 13-16 Oct 123+72=195; Sigma Dos 1-14 Oct 132-137 + 65-68 (197-205); SocioMetrica 10-11 Oct 141+64=205; GAD3 6-8 Oct 133+65=198; Hamalgama 5-8 Oct 144+68=212; EM 5-9 Oct 131+67=198; IMOP 5-7 Oct 130+70=200; CIS-Opina 1-6 Oct 119+67=186; CIS-Ateneo 119+66=185; EM 2-3 Oct 129+69=198; SocioMetrica 1-3 Oct 143+62=205; Data10 2 Oct 139+64=203.
- Party-commissioned polls: PSOE 5 Oct 126+71=197; PSOE 25 Oct poll has PSOE 30.0 vs PP 29.0 (vote shares only). The CIS raw barometer has PSOE ahead by 11.8 points.
- El Debate (Oct 25): 12 pollsters from 6 Sep to 9 Oct gave PP+Vox 198-212 seats, median 203; PP 129-147, Vox 62-70.
- Trend: PP vote share is down from about 35% in 2024 to 31-32%; Vox is up from 11% to about 19%. Late-October polls show PP slightly softer (IMOP 28.5%, EM 30.9%).
- Resolves off official Congress results for PP + Vox seats (which coalition partners count as PP has not been checked).
- Event window: single election day, 29 Nov 2026. As of 25 Oct, 0% elapsed and the event is 35 days out.
- Searched but not found: a dedicated seat-total market, and late-October aggregate seat models (poliwave and democrata were blocked).
calls.reference_class: Spanish general elections 2015-2023: final-month poll seat projections vs actual right-bloc seats (error SD ~8-12 seats, 2023 overstated by ~12)

calls.reasoning: Oct 2026 private polls put PP+Vox ~186-214 (median ~199-203 across pollsters; latest Electomanía 194, IMOP 195, Votómetro 207). Late-October trend is mildly toward PSOE (PP slipping). Spanish polls have historically overstated PP+Vox (Apr 2019, 2023 by ~10-20 seats), Nov 2019 accurate. I shade median to ~193 and keep wide tails. Polymarket PP-most-seats at 0.78 (near-miss contract) implies non-trivial narrowing expected; no combined-seats market found.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Spanish general-election poll averages vs results for the PP+Vox bloc. Polls 6 Sep-9 Oct had PP+Vox at 198-212 (median 203). RTVE average 15 Oct: 202. Late-October polls are a bit lower: EM-Analytics 194-197, IMOP 195, Sigma Dos 197-205, GAD3 198 (Vox -4), and Sociometro 174 as a low outlier. In 2023 polls overstated the right bloc by roughly 6-10 seats (from memory, not re-checked this run) and the snap campaign may mobilise the left, so I shade about 10 below the average to a median near 190. Markets: Polymarket only prices PP winning the most seats (0.78, ~$77k volume), a near-miss contract with no PP+Vox seat-total market found. That is consistent with a PP lead but not an anchor.

calls.reference_class: Spanish general elections 2015-2023: final poll average of the right bloc vs actual seats (with the 2023 overestimate)

calls.reasoning: Late-October seat projections cluster at 194-198 (EM-Analytics 194-196, IMOP 195, GAD3 198, Sigma Dos 197-205). Sept-early Oct polls had a median of 203, and PP is slipping slightly. Polls overstated the right bloc in Apr 2019 and 2023 but were accurate in Nov 2019, so I shade about 5 seats to a median near 192. Wide tails reflect historical poll error. Polymarket's PP-most-seats at 0.78 is a near-miss contract: consistent with PP+Vox in the 180s-200s, but not an anchor.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the poll data (late Oct roughly 194-198, earlier median 203). They differ mainly on the size of the historical overstatement of the right bloc. Runs 1 and 2 said 10-15 seats in 2023; Run 3 said 6-10, unchecked. Runs 1 and 2 also agree that Apr 2019 was overstated by about 15-20 and Nov 2019 was accurate. With no web access I could not verify any of these error figures, so I treat the average overstatement as about 5-10 seats. Applied to a late-October center of about 196-197, that gives a median of about 192. Whether late PSOE mobilisation adds further downside is a judgment call; I think it is small. Polymarket's PP-most-seats contract is a near-miss and was not used as an anchor. No combined-seats market was found by any run.

disagreements.claim: Size of the 2023 poll overstatement of the PP+Vox bloc (6-10 vs 10-15 seats)
disagreements.verdict: Unverified this run (no web access). Runs 1 and 2 (10-15) and Run 3 (6-10, from memory and unchecked) differ, so it stays uncertain. I assume overstatement in the 6-15 range and fold it into a ~5-seat shade plus wide tails.

disagreements.claim: Which polls define the current center (late-Oct ~195 vs Sept-early Oct median 203)
disagreements.verdict: Weight the late-October readings more heavily: center about 196-197 before adjusting for historical error

disagreements.claim: How much to shade for left mobilisation in the snap campaign
disagreements.verdict: Small additional shade; median 192 sits between Run 3's 190 and Run 1's 195 on the evidence, not by averaging
About 3% each side, given the size of past poll misses
